findings.passage: Equal protection under the law is fundamental to a fair and functioning democracy. Every Virginian—regardless of race, religion, ethnicity, gender identity, sex, sexual orientation, ability, or age—deserves the freedom to live safely, be treated with dignity, and participate fully in civic life. My legislative work reflects this commitment, including votes to enshrine reproductive freedom, safeguard marriage equality, and restore voting rights so our democracy remains inclusive and accountable to the people it serves.
findings.note: Section 'Protecting equal rights and voting access' on her campaign priorities page; undated. Speaks of voting access and restoring voting rights in general terms, with no mention of ID or citizenship.

findings.motion: Read third time and passed House (62-Y 35-N 0-A)
findings.note: HB 773, absentee voting cure process: removes the rule that absentee ballots must arrive by the Friday before the election for errors to be cured, and moves the deadline to cure errors in absentee ballot applications to noon on the Monday after the election. She voted yes on House passage.

findings.motion: Read third time and passed House (92-Y 6-N 0-A)
findings.note: HB 78, elections administration: makes certifying results a ministerial duty of local electoral boards, with removal and civil penalty for refusal. She voted yes on House passage. Related election-law vote, not a voter ID vote.
